subject: Reserved GPU demo & capacity check for Vergence AI
messages:
From: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@vergence.ai>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Reserved GPU evaluation for high-throughput inference

Hi Diego,

I signed up for the self-serve trial yesterday and landed on Redwood after benchmarking latency on a few open models.
We are evaluating a dedicated/reserved setup for inference and would like a short technical demo focused on throughput and p95 latency.

Quick context:
- Company: Vergence AI (product analytics for streaming data)
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~80
- Typical sequence length: 350-600 tokens
- Target p95 generation latency: <= 200ms
- Expected daily tokens: ~1.2M
- Preferred region: us-west-2
- Model family we expect to use: gpt-open-13B-quant

Can we book a 45 minute walkthrough next week? Prefer mornings PST. I can bring our CTO (Jenna Park) and procurement for a brief pricing/terms discussion.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of ML, Vergence AI
alex.zhou@vergence.ai

Attachment: trial-output-sample.txt (text)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@vergence.ai>
Date: 2027-04-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Reserved GPU evaluation for high-throughput inference

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the context and for trying the self-serve flow — glad you surfaced the latency numbers early. I work on new accounts and will run the demo; I want to include our solutions engineer Marcus Lin to cover the kernel/quantization details and autoscaling patterns. I cc'd Marcus.

A few quick asks so we can tailor the walkthrough to your workload:
- Are those sequence lengths steady or do you have occasional spikes to 1k+ tokens?
- Is the 200ms p95 for end-to-end inference (network + generation) or server-side generation only?
- Any hard constraints on cold-start latency versus warmed KV cache behavior?

Available 45 minute slots (PST mornings) next week:
- Tue 2027-04-13, 09:30 - 10:15
- Wed 2027-04-14, 08:30 - 09:15
- Thu 2027-04-15, 10:00 - 10:45

If those don't work, propose two slots and I will coordinate. I attached our pre-demo checklist (MA-Checklist.pdf) — if you can fill a couple of items (sample requests, preferred model config) that helps Marcus prepare perf numbers and a short perf-run we can show live.

Also linking our reserved-capacity quickstart so you can skim before the call: https://docs.redwood.ai/demos/reserved-gpu-quickstart

Best,
Diego Fernandez
SDR, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com

Attachment: MA-Checklist.pdf (PDF)

From: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@vergence.ai>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Jenna Park <jenna.park@vergence.ai>
Date: 2027-04-05T12:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Reserved GPU evaluation for high-throughput inference

Thanks Diego — copying Jenna (CTO).

Answers:
- Sequence lengths are mostly 350-600 tokens with occasional longer outliers up to ~1k for certain ad-hoc analysis jobs.
- The p95 target is end-to-end from our frontend to final token. Network adds ~20-30ms typically, so server-side <170ms would be ideal.
- Warm cache behavior is important; cold-starts are acceptable if transient.

We prefer Wed 2027-04-14 08:30 PST if that slot is still open.

We also want the demo to cover:
- Autoscaling behavior under a sudden ramp (what policies you recommend for reserved pools)
- Quantization tradeoffs for gpt-open-13B-quant at our target latencies
- Example rollout plan for canarying model updates between hosted and dedicated variants

On pricing: can you include a brief overview of reserved commit levels and typical contract lengths you see for teams our size? Jenna and I will bring procurement questions.

I attached a small latency-sample.csv from our trial run so you can eyeball p50/p95.

Alex
Head of ML, Vergence AI

Attachment: latency-sample.csv (CSV)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@vergence.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jenna Park <jenna.park@vergence.ai>
Date: 2027-04-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Confirmed: Reserved GPU walkthrough (Wed 2027-04-14 08:30 PST)

Hi Alex and Jenna,

Great — Wed 2027-04-14, 08:30 - 09:15 PST is confirmed. I attached a calendar invite (calendar-invite.ics) and our pre-demo checklist (MA-Checklist.pdf) again. Please fill the checklist items you can; Marcus will use the sample requests to prepare a short perf run against a quantized 13B so we can show realistic p95 numbers.

Proposed agenda (45 minutes):
- 5 min intros and account goals
- 15 min perf: reserved pool sizing, p95 targets, autoscaling patterns
- 15 min demo: live perf run + KV cache walkthrough
- 5 min rollout & pricing overview (reserved commits, common contract lengths, SLA notes)
- 5 min Q&A / next steps

Related links:
- HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/contact/VER-2381
- Pre-demo checklist: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cMA-checklist

If you prefer a longer technical deep-dive for engineers we can schedule a follow-up with our PM and latency team. Looking forward to it.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
SDR, Redwood Inference
+1 (555) 555-0198
diego.fernandez@redwood.com

Attachments: calendar-invite.ics (ICS), MA-Checklist.pdf (PDF)
